terms.definition: A positively charged particle in the nucleus of an atom.
terms.function: Gives the atom its identity — its count defines the element.
terms.whereItIs: The red particles in the nucleus of the cutaway atom.
terms.whyItMatters: Protons are what make every element the element that it is.

terms.definition: The +1 electric charge carried by every proton.
terms.function: Gives the nucleus its positive charge and pulls the negative electrons toward it.
terms.whereItIs: On every proton in the model's nucleus.
terms.whyItMatters: Charge is what holds the atom together — positive protons pull negative electrons.

terms.definition: The element an atom belongs to, fixed by its proton count.
terms.function: Makes every element unique — no two elements share a proton count.
terms.whereItIs: The proton count highlighted in the model.
terms.whyItMatters: Element identity is the foundation of the whole periodic table.

terms.definition: The number of protons in an atom — the element's number on the periodic table.
terms.function: Orders the periodic table and identifies each element.
terms.whereItIs: Shown as the counted protons on the model.
terms.whyItMatters: Atomic number is the first number on every periodic table box.
